correctness.rationale: With n>=3, t>0 and each edge priced t on a distinguished perfect matching and one elsewhere, the strict convexity of tr(L+J/(2n))^-1 on connected Laplacians, injectivity of edge weights and automorphisms force a unique two-orbit global optimum. The exact spectrum {0,2[a+(n−1)b],(nb)^(n−1),[2a+(n−2)b]^(n−1)} gives K=2nΣλ^-1. Budget normalization gives the one-variable F. Its derivative at a=0 yields T_n, and convexity along a gives the unique deletion/interior regimes even at equality. Algebraic differentiation yields T_n>1, monotonicity and expansion. Minimizer control for x/n and the derivative expansion at t=1+s/n prove all asymptotics. Exact Python Fraction checker verified 140 rational matrix-inverse/spectrum/budget identities, 75 endpoint comparisons, 23 window checks, 216 nonsymmetric feasible competitors. Finite checks do not prove the theorem; analytical proof independently addresses all integer n>=3 and real t>0.

value.rationale: The matched complete-bipartite graph is a natural redundant-interconnection topology, with a distinguished class of potentially costly links and explicit total investment constraint. Its priced connectivity decision is not determined by the well-known unweighted crown Kirchhoff index; a sharp, n-dependent deletion threshold, full unique conductance allocation and shrinking t=1+O(1/n) window give structural/operational information over every n>=3. This is a complete natural decision classification and not a renamed graph invariant, arbitrary finite slice or routine tabular recomputation. The exact parameter n=3, t=3 predicts all costly matches deleted whereas equal price t=1 retains them.
